unit_title: Lifetime Activity Audit and Adult Transition Planning
standards: Michigan PE Standard 5: Recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction. [Michigan PE Grades 9-12 LEVEL 2 (advanced/elective high-school physical education)]

Michigan PE Standard 3: Demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical fitness. [Michigan PE Grades 9-12 LEVEL 2 (advanced/elective high-school physical education)]
Michigan PE Standard 4: Exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others. [Michigan PE Grades 9-12 LEVEL 2 (advanced/elective high-school physical education)]

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of auditing current activities against post-graduation reality in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe time, money, transport, facility, and social access after high school using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply what disappears when school activity structures end in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving activities that require nothing but space and time; correct it and explain why.
Connect building a minimum viable activity week with setting a realistic first-year activity commitment and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Audit every activity the learner currently does against post-graduation constraints, then design a minimum viable activity week that would survive the worst plausible version of next year.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with safe, independent application and adequate explanation of cues, tactics, or training reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84% or inconsistent explanation; assign varied practice and a fresh transfer check on a later occasion.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the simplest version and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source on one occasion, not the sole basis for long-term mastery. Never adjust a score for body size, weight, or appearance.

accommodation_note: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
inclusion_note: No household income, address, or family financial detail is entered into course records; cost planning uses general figures the learner supplies at whatever precision they choose.
